q: Compared to Groups 1-7, which typically involve designing part or all of a building's overall architecture, Group VIII projects are best characterized as
o: identical in scope, just billed differently
broader in scope, always covering multiple buildings on one site
limited strictly to structural engineering
narrower in scope, focused on detail-level components, fittings, or interior/development work rather than the whole building
n: Group VIII is scope-limited to detail-level design work (built-ins, fittings, screens, counters, interiors, development planning), which is why it is billed as a flat percentage rather than by building classification or unit count. (Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.8)

q: Which of the following would NOT be classified under Building Type Group VIII (Extensive Detail)?
o: Design of a screen wall and reception counter for a building lobby
Design of the complete architectural and structural shell of a new hospital building
Design of built-in equipment and special fittings for a commercial space
Architectural interior design services for a tenant space
n: Designing a complete new building's shell/structure is full building design falling under Groups 1-7's classification-based or unit-based scales, not the extensive-detail scope of Group VIII. (Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.8)

q: An architect is engaged solely to design custom built-in cabinetry and storage elements for a residential unit, with a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of PHP 800,000.00 for that built-in scope. Applying the Group VIII rate, what is the RPF?
n: RPF = 15% x PCC = 0.15 x PHP 800,000.00 = PHP 120,000.00. Built-in cabinetry/storage components fall under Group VIII's flat 15% of PCC rate. (Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.8)
scenario: An architect is engaged solely to design custom built-in cabinetry and storage elements for a residential unit, with a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of PHP 800,000.00 for that built-in scope.

q: An architect is engaged only to design built-in kitchen cabinetry and millwork for a house whose overall architectural and structural design was already completed by another firm. Under SPP Doc. 202, how should this engagement be classified for fee purposes?
o: Under Groups 1-6, using the bracket scale for successive buildings
Under Group 7, using the housing-unit tiered scale
Under Group 9, with a 150% surcharge on the base RPF
Under Group VIII, at a flat 15% of the PCC attributable to the built-in/millwork scope
n: Because the engagement is limited to built-in components/elements rather than the building's overall design, it falls under Group VIII and is billed at the flat 15% of PCC for that detail-level scope — not under the building-classification or unit-based scales used for full building design. (Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.8)

q: A landowner engages an architect strictly for a development planning/masterplanning engagement over a parcel of raw land, before any building design is commissioned, with a PCC of PHP 5,000,000.00 attributed to that development-planning scope. What is the RPF?
n: RPF = 15% x PCC = 0.15 x PHP 5,000,000.00 = PHP 750,000.00. Development planning and/or design is expressly listed under Group VIII. (Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.8)
scenario: A landowner engages an architect strictly for a development planning/masterplanning engagement over a parcel of raw land, before any building design is commissioned, with a PCC of PHP 5,000,000.00 attributed to that development-planning scope.

q: Why does SPP Doc. 202 assign Group VIII a single flat percentage RPF (15% of PCC) instead of a bracket or tiered table like Groups 1-7 use?
o: Because Group VIII projects are always larger in PCC than any Group 1-7 project
Because Group VIII is reserved exclusively for government projects

Because Group VIII projects are typically limited, detail-level scopes (built-ins, fittings, counters, interiors, development planning) rather than whole-building designs whose fee would otherwise need to scale with building classification or number of units/buildings
Because Group VIII fees are fixed by law and cannot be a percentage of PCC
n: The bracket/tiered tables in Groups 1-7 exist to scale fees with the complexity of designing whole buildings (classification, successive buildings, or number of housing units). Because Group VIII covers narrower, detail-level scopes rather than whole-building design, a single flat percentage of PCC is used instead. (Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.8)

q: Under SPP Document 202 (Regular Design Services), what kind of engagement does Building Type Group VIII cover?
o: Alterations, renovations, retrofitting, and expansion of an existing building
Full architectural and engineering design of a new low- to medium-rise building

Projects involving extensive detail, such as designs for built-in components or elements, built-in equipment, special fittings, screens, counters, architectural interiors, and development planning and/or design
Rendering a professional opinion, advice, or clarification on a technical matter
n: Group VIII is defined precisely as covering extensive-detail scopes — built-in components/elements, built-in equipment, special fittings, screens, counters, architectural interiors, and development planning and/or design — not full-building design (Groups 1-7), alteration work (Group 9), or advisory opinion (Group 10). (Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.8)

q: How does the RPF computation method for Group VIII differ structurally from that of Groups 1 to 7?
o: Group VIII has no RPF at all; fees are negotiated case by case
Group VIII uses a tiered scale based on the number of housing units, exactly like Group 7
Group VIII uses a scale that decreases with each additional building, exactly like Groups 1-6
Group VIII uses a single flat percentage of PCC, while Groups 1-7 use fee scales that vary by building classification, number of buildings, or number of housing units
n: Groups 1-6 scale RPF by successive buildings (100%/50%/40%/30% of RPF for 1st/2nd/3rd/4th+ buildings) and Group 7 scales by number of housing units, both varying with project scope. Group VIII instead applies one flat percentage (15% of PCC) with no bracket or tier. (Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.8)

q: A developer engages an architect solely to prepare a masterplan (site development planning and design) for a proposed mixed-use estate, with no building design yet commissioned. Under SPP Doc. 202, which Group and rate apply to this engagement?
o: Group 9, since it precedes construction
Group VIII, at a flat 15% of the PCC for the development-planning scope
Group 7, at 10% of the PCC as a first housing unit
Group 10, since masterplanning is merely advisory opinion
n: Development planning and/or design is expressly named as a Group VIII scope, billed at the flat 15% of the PCC attributed to that engagement — it is not an advisory opinion (Group 10) nor a housing-unit design (Group 7). (Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.8)

q: Which set of project types is explicitly listed under Group VIII as qualifying for the flat 15% of PCC rate?
o: Additions and expansions to an existing school building
Single-detached houses, duplexes, and row houses
Housing projects using one set of plans across multiple units on one site
Built-in components or elements, built-in equipment, special fittings, screens, counters, architectural interiors, and development planning and/or design
n: Sec. 6.3.8 lists exactly these extensive-detail scopes for Group VIII; the other options describe Group 7 (housing projects, one set of plans across units) or Group 9 (alterations/additions to existing buildings). (Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.8)

q: An architectural firm is engaged to (1) renovate the facade and structural elements of an existing five-year-old commercial building and, under a separate scope, (2) design new built-in reception counters and interior screens for the same building. How should RPF be computed for the two scopes?
o: No RPF applies to either scope because the building already exists
The entire engagement is billed at a single flat 15% of the combined PCC

The renovation scope is computed under Group 9 (increase of 50%, i.e., a total of 150% of the applicable base RPF), while the built-in counters/screens scope is computed separately under Group VIII's flat 15% of its own PCC
Both scopes are billed under Group 7's housing-unit scale
n: Renovation of an existing building falls under Group 9, whose RPF is increased by 50% (total 150% of the RPF otherwise applicable). The built-in counters and interior screens are a separate, extensive-detail scope governed by Group VIII's flat 15% of the PCC attributable to that scope. (Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.8)

q: A homeowner separately hires an architect to design special fittings (custom window grilles and hardware details) for a residence, with a PCC of PHP 450,000.00 for that fittings scope. What RPF applies?
n: RPF = 15% x PCC = 0.15 x PHP 450,000.00 = PHP 67,500.00. Special fittings are expressly listed under Group VIII. (Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.8)
scenario: A homeowner separately hires an architect to design special fittings (custom window grilles and hardware details) for a residence, with a PCC of PHP 450,000.00 for that fittings scope.

q: In distinguishing whether a given architectural engagement falls under Group VIII rather than under the full-building Groups 1-7, what is the key determining factor?
o: The number of stories in the building
The geographic location of the project
The total floor area of the building involved

Whether the engagement is limited to detail-level scopes (built-ins, fittings, screens, counters, interiors, or development planning) rather than the building's overall architectural/structural design
n: Group VIII is defined by the nature of the scope — extensive detail work — not by size, location, or height. If the engagement covers the whole building's design, Groups 1-7 (or 9, if it is an existing building) apply instead. (Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.8)

q: In Group VIII, the phrase "development planning and/or design" is best understood as referring to
o: construction supervision of an ongoing project
structural engineering design of a building's frame
a scope such as site/master development planning or design work, engaged separately from full building design
quantity surveying and cost estimating services
n: Alongside built-in components, equipment, fittings, screens, counters, and interiors, Group VIII's list includes development planning and/or design as its own qualifying scope of detail-level or planning-level work distinct from designing an entire building. (Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.8)

q: What is the overall purpose of dividing Regular Design Services into Building Type Groups (Groups 1 through 10) under SPP Doc. 202?
o: To categorize the architect's recommended professional fee basis according to the nature, scale, and complexity of the project or scope of engagement
To determine which projects require a building permit
To assign each Group to a different government agency for approval
To limit which projects a licensed architect is legally allowed to accept
n: The Building Type Groups classify projects and scopes of architectural engagement (by building classification, unit count, extensive detail, alteration, or advisory opinion, among others) so that the Recommended Professional Fee can be computed on a basis appropriate to that project's nature and complexity — Group VIII being the flat-rate category for extensive-detail work. (Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.8)

q: A commercial building owner separately engages an architect to design a decorative lobby screen wall, with a PCC of PHP 1,200,000.00 for that screen-wall scope alone. Using the Group VIII flat rate, compute the RPF.
n: RPF = 15% x PCC = 0.15 x PHP 1,200,000.00 = PHP 180,000.00. A decorative screen is expressly listed under Group VIII. (Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.8)
scenario: A commercial building owner separately engages an architect to design a decorative lobby screen wall, with a PCC of PHP 1,200,000.00 for that screen-wall scope alone.

q: A retail tenant hires an architect purely to design the architectural interiors (finishes, partitions, ceiling, and interior fit-out) of its leased space, with a PCC of PHP 3,500,000.00 for that interior fit-out scope. Compute the RPF using Group VIII.
n: RPF = 15% x PCC = 0.15 x PHP 3,500,000.00 = PHP 525,000.00. Architectural interiors are expressly listed under Group VIII. (Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.8)
scenario: A retail tenant hires an architect purely to design the architectural interiors (finishes, partitions, ceiling, and interior fit-out) of its leased space, with a PCC of PHP 3,500,000.00 for that interior fit-out scope.

q: A property owner hires an architect only to redesign the reception counter and interior screens of an existing office lobby, with no changes to the building's structure or overall architectural layout. Which Group governs the fee for this engagement?
o: Group I, since it is still architectural work
Group 10, since it is merely advisory
Group VIII, since the scope is limited to counters and screens (extensive detail)
Group 9, since any work on an existing building is automatically an alteration
n: Because the scope is confined to a counter and screens — both explicitly named in Group VIII — and does not touch the building's structure or overall design, it is billed under Group VIII's flat 15% of PCC rather than as an alteration under Group 9. (Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.8)

q: What is the Recommended Professional Fee (RPF) for Building Type Group VIII (Extensive Detail) projects?
o: 150% of the RPF otherwise applicable, as with Group 9 alterations
A flat 15% of the PCC
6% of the PCC, as with Detailed Architectural Design Services under Group 7
10% of the Project Construction Cost (PCC), as with a first housing unit under Group 7
n: Group VIII's RPF is a single flat rate: 15% of the Project Construction Cost (PCC), regardless of project size or building classification. (Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.8)

q: An architect designs a reception counter and millwork package for an office lobby, with a PCC of PHP 650,000.00 for that package. What RPF applies under Group VIII?
n: RPF = 15% x PCC = 0.15 x PHP 650,000.00 = PHP 97,500.00. Counters are expressly listed under Group VIII. (Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.8)
scenario: An architect designs a reception counter and millwork package for an office lobby, with a PCC of PHP 650,000.00 for that package.

q: How does Group VIII's flat 15% of PCC compare with the RPF treatment under the adjoining Groups 9 and 10?
o: Group 10 uses the same successive-building scale as Groups 1-6
Groups 9 and 10 both use the identical flat 15% of PCC rate as Group VIII

Group 9 (alterations/renovations to existing Group 1-5 buildings) increases the applicable base RPF by 50% (to a total of 150%), while Group 10 (rendering opinion/advice on technical matters) is treated differently from a straightforward percentage-of-PCC fee — distinct from Group VIII's own flat 15% of PCC for extensive-detail scopes
Group 9 uses a housing-unit tiered scale identical to Group 7
n: Group 9 covers alterations/renovations/retrofit/expansion of existing buildings under Groups 1-5, with RPF increased by 50% for a total of 150% of the otherwise-applicable RPF. Group 10 covers advisory opinion/advice, which is not computed as a straightforward percentage-of-PCC design fee. Group VIII stands apart from both, applying its own flat 15% of PCC to extensive-detail scopes. (Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.8)

q: Within SPP Document 202's ten Building Type Groups (Groups 1 to 10), where does Group VIII fit in the overall scheme?
o: It is the extensive-detail group, distinct from the full-building design groups (1-7), the alteration/renovation group (9), and the advisory-opinion group (10)
It is the housing-project group scaled by number of units
It is one of the groups (1-6) differentiated by classification of new buildings by successive-building scale
It applies only to government infrastructure projects
n: Groups 1-6 classify new buildings and scale RPF by successive buildings; Group 7 covers multi-unit housing projects; Group VIII covers extensive-detail scopes at a flat 15% of PCC; Group 9 covers alterations/renovations at 150% of the base RPF; Group 10 covers advisory opinions. Group VIII sits between the full-building groups and the alteration/advisory groups as its own distinct category. (Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.8)

q: An architect is engaged only to design built-in equipment (e.g., custom fabricated fixtures) for a restaurant, with a PCC of PHP 2,000,000.00 for that built-in-equipment scope. Compute the Group VIII RPF.
n: RPF = 15% x PCC = 0.15 x PHP 2,000,000.00 = PHP 300,000.00. Built-in equipment is expressly listed under Group VIII. (Source: SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.8)
scenario: An architect is engaged only to design built-in equipment (e.g., custom fabricated fixtures) for a restaurant, with a PCC of PHP 2,000,000.00 for that built-in-equipment scope.
